narration: Colour returns first to the Data Preparation stage on the left. A reference frame from the video is annotated with coloured boxes marking the hands and the object being held.
Next, the preparation steps light up: the held object is replaced with a new product image, boxes are detected on the input frame, and the hand mesh is augmented to vary the grasp.
The Training Pipeline panel takes on colour. The reference image is pushed through a frozen VAE encoder to obtain its latent representation.
The Reference U-Net appears in green. Its stack of self-attention layers extracts appearance features that are injected downstream into the denoising network.
On the lower branch, layout guidance frames are encoded by the layout encoder and added to sampled noise, giving the spatial conditioning signal.
The Denoising U-Net fills in. Green self-attention blocks carry the reference appearance while blue temporal-attention blocks keep the generated frames consistent over time.
ControlNet turns yellow. It consumes the rendered hand mesh sequence and feeds pose control into the denoising backbone.

The HOI Restoration Module is revealed. Hand and object attention blocks query hand and object texture memory banks through cross-attention, and the results are masked and added back into the features.
Finally the output path regains colour: the frozen VAE decoder converts the denoised latents into the generated frames, showing the person holding the replaced object.
